17:1.sourceText: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ Ἀνένδεκτόν ἐστιν τοῦ τὰ σκάνδαλα μὴ ἐλθεῖν, οὐαὶ δὲ δι’ οὗ ἔρχεται·
17:1.targetText: And He said to the disciples, “It is impossible for the stumbling blocks not to come, but woe [to him] through whom they come;

groups.note: The actual articular-infinitive frame contains stumbling blocks as its accusative subject. English introduces that same infinitival subject with for; no independent Greek for preposition is invented.

The actual free-relative person οὗ identifies the one through whom the stumbling comes, also the person addressed by woe. English states that same person first as [to him] and then whom; no second written Greek personal pronoun or to preposition is claimed.
Actual ἔρχεται is singular, agreeing with the neuter-plural stumbling-block subject in Greek. English uses plural they come for that same subject; no plural Greek verb form is substituted.

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 explicitly identifies the disciples as His with αὐτοῦ. TR and LSV omit that separately written possessive here.

17:2.sourceText: λυσιτελεῖ αὐτῷ εἰ λίθος μυλικὸς περίκειται περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔρριπται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ἢ ἵνα σκανδαλίσῃ τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ἕνα.
17:2.targetText: it is more profitable to him if a weighty millstone is put around his neck, and he has been cast into the sea, than that he may cause one of these little ones to stumble.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV describes the millstone as weighty. N1904 prints generic stone + mill-related adjective, whereas TR has the donkey-mill expression μύλος ὀνικός; no weight adjective or donkey lemma is assigned to the actual N1904 words.

17:3.sourceText: προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς. ἐὰν ἁμάρτῃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου, ἐπιτίμησον αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐὰν μετανοήσῃ, ἄφες αὐτῷ.
17:3.targetText: Take heed to yourselves, and if your brother may sin in regard to you, rebuke him, and if he may change his mind, forgive him,

groups.note: Actual μετανοήσῃ is the single repenting/change-of-mind predicate. English states its meaning as he may change his mind; no separate Greek mind noun or possessive is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly connects the if-sin clause with δέ, represented by English and. Pinned N1904 begins that conditional directly with ἐάν.
TR explicitly includes εἰς σέ in the sin clause. Pinned N1904 has no separately written personal sin-target phrase here.

17:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ καὶ ἑπτάκις ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς σὲ λέγων Μετανοῶ, ἀφήσεις αὐτῷ.
17:4.targetText: and if seven times in the day he may sin against you, and seven times in the day may return to you, saying, I change my mind, you will forgive him.”

groups.note: One actual temporal genitive τῆς ἡμέρας supplies the day unit for the immediately coordinated sevenfold sin/return condition. English repeats in the day with both counts, as TR explicitly does; no second written N1904 day phrase or independent ἐν is claimed.
Actual μετανοῶ is the single first-person change-of-mind/repent predicate. English expands that actual verb without separately printed Greek mind/possessive words.

17:5.sourceText: Καὶ εἶπαν οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ Κυρίῳ Πρόσθες ἡμῖν πίστιν.
17:5.targetText: And the apostles said to the LORD, “Add to us faith”;

17:6.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος Εἰ ἔχετε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐλέγετε ἂν τῇ συκαμίνῳ ταύτῃ Ἐκριζώθητι καὶ φυτεύθητι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· καὶ ὑπήκουσεν ἂν ὑμῖν.
17:6.targetText: and the LORD said, “If you had faith as a grain of mustard, you would have said to this sycamine, Be uprooted, and be planted in the sea, and it would have obeyed you.

groups.note: Actual ἔχετε is present indicative you-have in N1904. English had follows the TR imperfect εἴχετε wording; the shared possession head is linked while the actual source tense remains explicit.
Actual imperfect saying verb plus ἄν forms the modal/counterfactual saying construction. English realizes that combination as you would have said; no independent Greek have auxiliary is invented.

17:7.sourceText: Τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν δοῦλον ἔχων ἀροτριῶντα ἢ ποιμαίνοντα, ὃς εἰσελθόντι ἐκ τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ Εὐθέως παρελθὼν ἀνάπεσε,
17:7.targetText: But who is he of you—having a servant plowing or feeding—who, to him having come in out of the field, will say, Having come, recline at once?

groups.note: Actual τίς identifies the interrogated person. English expands that personal question into who ... he; the extra English copula is separately identified as supplied, without inventing a Greek personal pronoun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in who-is-he. Pinned N1904 directly asks which person without a separately written be verb.

17:8.sourceText: ἀλλ’ οὐχὶ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ Ἑτοίμασον τί δειπνήσω, καὶ περιζωσάμενος διακόνει μοι ἕως φάγω καὶ πίω, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα φάγεσαι καὶ πίεσαι σύ;
17:8.targetText: But will not [rather] say to him, Prepare what I may dine, and having girded yourself around, minister to me, until I eat and drink, and after these things you will eat and drink?

groups.note: Actual ἀλλά is the corrective but/rather connective. English states both But and [rather] for that one correction; no Greek μᾶλλον comparative is claimed.
Actual middle περιζωσάμενος supplies the girding-oneself action. English yourself realizes that middle action, without a separately written source reflexive pronoun.

17:9.sourceText: μὴ ἔχει χάριν τῷ δούλῳ ὅτι ἐποίησεν τὰ διαταχθέντα;
17:9.targetText: Does he have favor to that servant because he did the things directed? I think not.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual μή marks a negative-expectation question. English prints an unnegated Does-he-have question and then a separately added I-think-not response; the question particle is not reassigned to a written opinion predicate.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly adds demonstrative ἐκείνῳ to the servant phrase. Pinned N1904 has the definite servant phrase without that separately written demonstrative.
TR adds the explicit οὐ δοκῶ response. Pinned N1904 ends with the question and has no separately printed thinking/negative-response clause.

17:10.sourceText: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ποιήσητε πάντα τὰ διαταχθέντα ὑμῖν, λέγετε ὅτι Δοῦλοι ἀχρεῖοί ἐσμεν, ὃ ὠφείλομεν ποιῆσαι πεποιήκαμεν.
17:10.targetText: So also you, when you may have done all the things directed you, say, We are unprofitable servants, because that which we owed to do we have done.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual first ὅτι introduces the quoted We-are-servants statement. English uses direct speech without a separate quotation that; this source marker is not moved into the later causal slot.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR has a second ὅτι introducing the because-what-we-owed explanation. Pinned N1904 directly begins that explanation with the relative ὃ, without a separately written causal conjunction.

17:11.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ, καὶ αὐτὸς διήρχετο διὰ μέσον Σαμαρίας καὶ Γαλιλαίας.
17:11.targetText: And it came to pass, in His going on to Jerusalem, that He passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee,

groups.note: Actual καί introduces the main passing clause under the came-to-pass temporal frame. English realizes that clause connection as that; no source ὅτι is invented.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly supplies accusative αὐτόν as subject of the going infinitive. Pinned N1904 has the going frame without that separately written personal subject; the later main-clause αὐτός remains attached to He there.

17:12.sourceText: καὶ εἰσερχομένου αὐτοῦ εἴς τινα κώμην ἀπήντησαν δέκα λεπροὶ ἄνδρες, οἳ ἔστησαν πόρρωθεν,

TR explicitly adds αὐτῷ as the meeting recipient. Pinned N1904 has no separately written recipient at met; its earlier αὐτοῦ is the differently attached entering subject.

17:13.sourceText: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦραν φωνὴν λέγοντες Ἰησοῦ Ἐπιστάτα, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς.
17:13.targetText: and they lifted up the voice, saying, “Jesus, Master, deal kindly with us”;

17:14.sourceText: καὶ ἰδὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες ἐπιδείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν. καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτοὺς ἐκαθαρίσθησαν.
17:14.targetText: and having seen [them], He said to them, “Having gone on, show yourselves to the priests”; and it came to pass, in their going, they were cleansed,

groups.note: Actual αὐτοῖς identifies the addressed group, the same immediately seen group in the coordinated seeing/saying actions. English repeats those people as [them] and to them; no extra written Greek accusative object pronoun or different group is claimed.
Actual accusative αὐτούς is the personal subject of the going infinitive. English nominalizes that frame as their going; no Greek genitive possessive form is substituted.

17:15.sourceText: εἷς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν, ἰδὼν ὅτι ἰάθη, ὑπέστρεψεν μετὰ φωνῆς μεγάλης δοξάζων τὸν Θεόν,

17:17.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Οὐχ οἱ δέκα ἐκαθαρίσθησαν; οἱ δὲ ἐννέα ποῦ;

17:19.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀναστὰς πορεύου· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.

17:20.targetText: And having been questioned by the Pharisees when the Kingdom of God comes, He answered them and said, “The Kingdom of God does not come with observation;

17:22.sourceText: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς Ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ὅτε ἐπιθυμήσετε μίαν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἰδεῖν καὶ οὐκ ὄψεσθε.
17:22.targetText: And He said to His disciples, “Days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man and you will not behold [it];

unmappedTarget.reason: English explicitly identifies the disciples as His. Neither pinned N1904 nor the checked TR prints a separate personal possessive with disciples in this verse.

17:27.targetText: they were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the Ark, and the flood came, and destroyed all;
